text.p: Former Bogota Mayor Antanas Mockus has launched what aides called his "pay-for-view" bid for the presidency by charging $5,500 to do an interview with Colombia's top news magazine.

Mockus, who abandoned the mayor's office earlier this month to launch an independent campaign for the country's top job, announced last week that he would help finance it by charging hard cash for any future interviews.
Several media outlets, including Bogota's leading newspaper El Tiempo, ridiculed the move and said they would not pay anything for comments from the self-described "neo-anarchist."

But Semana, the country's leading weekly news magazine, ran an interview with Mockus in its editions published on Monday in which Mockus proudly announced he was charging the publication $5,500. The amount was calculated based on what Semana charges for advertising space.
The interview ran alongside a picture of Mockus giving a thumbs up with one hand and clutching a fat wad of bank notes in the other.
Mockus, an academic and political outsider until his election as mayor in 1994, has been likened by some pundits to Peru's President Alberto Fujimori.

Recent polls show him riding a wave of popularity, thanks to a growing sense of disgust with politics as usual in Colombia. The country is torn by runaway levels of corruption and violence, and politics have been dominated by two traditional parties for more than four decades.
